prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Surrounded by bone, surrounded by cells, by rings, by rings of hell, by hair, surrounded by air-is-a-thing, surrounded by silhouette, by honey-wet bees, yet by skeletons of trees, surrounded by actual, yes, for practical purposes, people, surrounded by surreal popcorn, surrounded by the reborn: Surrender in the center to surroundings. O surrender forever, never end her, let her blend around, surrender to the surroundings that surround the tender endo-surrender, that tumble through the tumbling to that blue that curls around the crumbling, to that, the blue that rumbles under the sun bounding the pearl that we walk on, talk on; we can chalk that up to experience, sensing the brown here that’s blue now, a drop of water surrounding a cow that’s black & white, the warbling Blackburnian twitter that’s machining midnight orange in the light that’s glittering in the light green visible wind. That’s the ticket to the tunnel through the thicket that’s a cricket’s funnel of music to correct & pick it out from under the wing that whirls up over & out.

prompts.L3:
Please expand the following bullet points into a complete, well-structured text:

- The speaker emphasizes being surrounded by many layers of physical, natural, and surreal elements.
- The text presents surrender as a central response to the overwhelming presence of surroundings.
- Natural imagery such as trees, bees, water, birds, sunlight, and wind creates a vivid, shifting environment.
- The poem blends concrete reality with dreamlike and abstract language to evoke immersion in the world.
- Sound, motion, and color are used to suggest a living, musical landscape.
prompts.L4:
Please expand the following two-sentence summary into a complete text:

The text explores the self’s immersion in layered natural, bodily, and surreal surroundings through a rhythmic, associative cascade of images and wordplay. It suggests that surrendering to this enveloping world reveals interconnectedness and transforms perception into a vivid, musical experience.
prompts.L5:
Please write a text about the following topic:

Keywords: Surrounded, Surrender, Blackburnian

outputs.L1:
Surrounded by bone; surrounded by cells, by rings, by rings of hell, by hair; surrounded by air-as-a-thing, by silhouette, by honey-wet bees, yet by skeletons of trees; surrounded by the actual—yes, for practical purposes, people; surrounded by surreal popcorn; surrounded by the reborn: surrender, at the center, to surroundings.

O surrender forever; never end her. Let her blend around. Surrender to the surroundings that surround the tender endo-surrender, that tumble through the tumbling toward that blue that curls around the crumbling—to that blue that rumbles under the sun bounding the pearl we walk on, talk on. We can chalk that up to experience: sensing the brown here that is blue now, a drop of water surrounding a cow that is black and white; the warbling Blackburnian twitter machining midnight orange in the glittering light, in the light-green visible wind. That is the ticket to the tunnel through the thicket; that is a cricket’s funnel of music, to correct and pick it out from under the wing that whirls up, over, and out.
outputs.L2: Encased in bone and enclosed by living cells, by circles within circles, by infernal rings, by hair, by the fact that air itself has substance, by outlines and shadows, by bees damp with honey, and also by the bare frames of trees; enclosed, too, by real people—yes, in any practical sense—by dreamlike popcorn, and by those newly born again: yield at the middle to everything around you. Give in endlessly; do not finish her, but allow her to merge with what encircles her. Submit to the encompassing world that wraps the delicate inner yielding, the surrender that rolls through the rolling motion toward the blue, the blue that coils around what is falling apart, the blue that mutters beneath the sun as it borders the pearl-like earth we walk across and speak upon. We may count that as lived knowledge: feeling the brownness here that has become blue now, like a single water drop enclosing a black-and-white cow, while the wavering song of a Blackburnian bird chatters, turning midnight into orange machinery inside the glittering light, inside the pale green wind one can see. That is the pass into the passageway through the brush: a cricket-shaped channel of sound, meant to set things right and draw it out from beneath the wing that spins upward, over, and away.
outputs.L3:
The speaker emphasizes a feeling of being surrounded by many layers of physical, natural, and surreal elements. The world in the poem does not appear as a simple background, but as an active presence pressing in from every direction. Trees, bees, water, birds, sunlight, and wind all contribute to a dense and vivid environment. These details create the impression that the speaker is enclosed within a landscape that is constantly changing, moving, and alive.

In response to this overwhelming presence, surrender becomes a central idea. Rather than trying to resist or control the surrounding world, the speaker seems to give in to it. This surrender suggests an acceptance of being absorbed into the larger rhythms of nature and experience. The speaker’s identity appears to soften as the boundaries between the self and the environment become less distinct.

The poem’s natural imagery plays an important role in creating this sense of immersion. Trees may suggest rootedness and shelter, while bees introduce movement and sound. Water evokes flow and transformation, birds bring lightness and flight, and sunlight and wind add brightness, motion, and atmosphere. Together, these images form a shifting landscape that feels both physical and emotional.

At the same time, the poem blends concrete reality with dreamlike and abstract language. The recognizable elements of nature are presented in ways that feel surreal, as if the speaker is experiencing the world through heightened perception or a dream state. This mixture of the real and the unreal helps convey the intensity of the speaker’s experience. The landscape is not merely observed; it is felt as something mysterious, expansive, and deeply enveloping.

Sound, motion, and color further strengthen the sense of a living, musical world. The buzzing of bees, the movement of water, the flight of birds, the play of sunlight, and the force of wind all suggest a landscape filled with rhythm and energy. These sensory details make the poem feel dynamic rather than still. The world becomes almost musical, with each natural element contributing to a larger harmony. Through this rich combination of imagery and sensation, the poem evokes the experience of surrendering to a powerful, animated, and immersive environment.
outputs.L4:
The self is not presented as separate from the world, standing at a distance and observing it, but as something continually absorbed into its surroundings. Nature presses close from every side: earth, water, air, vegetation, weather, and animal presence all seem to gather around the speaker until the boundary between inner life and outer landscape begins to dissolve. The body, too, becomes part of this environment. Sensation replaces detached thought. Skin, breath, pulse, mouth, muscle, and memory mingle with leaves, mud, light, roots, waves, and wind, so that the self appears less like a fixed identity and more like a living surface through which the world passes.

This immersion is conveyed through a rapid, rhythmic flow of images. One perception leads to another by association rather than by strict logic. A sound becomes a color; a movement becomes a bodily feeling; a natural object turns suddenly strange, dreamlike, or symbolic. The language creates a cascade in which meanings overlap and transform. Wordplay, repetition, and musical phrasing make the text feel almost incantatory, as if thought itself were being carried forward by rhythm. The result is not a simple description of nature, but an experience of being surrounded, overwhelmed, and remade by it.

The surroundings are layered and shifting. They are at once natural, physical, and surreal. Familiar elements of the world appear with intensified vividness, while ordinary perception gives way to something more fluid and visionary. The landscape is not merely a setting; it behaves like an active force, drawing the self inward and outward at the same time. The speaker seems to sink into the environment, but this sinking is also an awakening. By surrendering control, the self discovers a wider network of connections: between body and earth, sound and sensation, movement and thought, the individual and the living world.

In this way, the text suggests that surrender is not a loss but a transformation. To yield to the enveloping world is to perceive more fully. The self becomes porous, receptive, and alive to correspondences that would otherwise remain hidden. Perception turns musical, not because it abandons meaning, but because it discovers meaning through rhythm, resonance, and relation. Everything seems to echo everything else. The world becomes a composition of touch, sound, image, and motion, and the self becomes one vibrating element within that larger harmony.
outputs.L5:
Surrounded by the hush of an early autumn forest, the small Blackburnian warbler flashed like a spark among the dark branches. Its fiery orange throat glowed against the green canopy, a brief and brilliant sign of life before the season turned cold.

For a moment, everything seemed to surrender to its presence: the wind softened, the leaves stilled, and even the shadows appeared to pause. The bird did not struggle against the changing sky or the coming migration. It simply followed the ancient rhythm written into its wings.

In that quiet scene, surrounded by fading light and falling leaves, the Blackburnian became more than a bird. It was a reminder that surrender is not always defeat. Sometimes it is trust—trust in the journey, in instinct, and in the unseen path ahead.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a surreal prose poem centered on the word “surrounded,” using dense repetition, internal rhyme, and associative imagery involving bone, bees, trees, water, birds, and light.
counterfactuals.output:
**Surrounded**

Surrounded, I said, and the word became a room of bone.  
Surrounded, and the bone began to bloom—white broom, moon-comb, tomb-limb—  
a ribcage ringing with bees, bees in the knees of the trees,  
bees in the blown-open bells of my elbows,  
bees making honey of the hollow.

Surrounded by trees, by the green teeth of trees,  
by trees that drink dark water and dream upward,  
root-tongued, rain-wronged, leaf-lit, light-bitten.  
Their branches are antlers, their antlers are rivers,  
their rivers are birds that remember being water.  
Every bird is a cup of light spilled from a skull.  
Every skull is a nest. Every nest is a question  
feathered and weathered and wet.

Surrounded, surrounded: the sound goes round,  
a drowned crown, a wound wound tight with shining.  
Water walks through the walls wearing mirrors.  
Water with its blue bones, its stone-throat, its throat-note,  
its endless yes and no in the undertow.  
I kneel to drink and swallow a flock.  
Inside me, wings begin their small bright riots.

The bees return, gold ghosts in the orchard of my ribs.  
They hum: bone is only frozen light,  
light is only water remembering fire,  
fire is only a bird with no body,  
and the body is only a tree surrounded by weather.  
Surrounded by weather, whether I wither or flower,  
I hear the hairline fractures singing sap,  
hear the marrow’s narrow river glitter and gnaw.

O surrounded, round sound, surrounder, surrender—  
I am ringed by wings, by stings, by things that sing  
without mouths: the birch’s pale wrist, the heron’s hinge,  
the rain’s thin pins, the pond’s blind eye.  
Bone-bee, tree-sea, bird-word, light-white—  
all of it circling, all of it thirsting,  
all of it making a halo of hunger around me.

And at the center of surrounded,  
where the sound is most round, most wound, most water,  
I find not myself but a door of bees,  
a tree of birds, a bone of light,  
and beyond it, more surrounding:  
water around the bone, bone around the bee,  
bee around the blossom, blossom around the bird,  
bird around the bright, bright void—  
and the void, too, humming,  
surrounded.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a single flowing paragraph in the style of experimental language poetry, beginning with “Surrounded by bone,” and evolving into a meditation on surrendering to one’s surroundings.
counterfactuals.output: Surrounded by bone, the room learns my outline before I do, white hinge and hush, a ribbed alphabet spelling enclosure as invitation, as weather, as the soft machinery of being held; I press my ear to the walls and hear not prison but pulse, not boundary but breathing, the world repeating itself in mineral syllables, cup, dust, window, skin, until resistance loosens its bright knot and I become less a figure than a listening, less a will than a field, letting the chair enter me with its wooden patience, the floor with its flat theology, the dim light with its yellow animal moving slowly across my hands; to surrender is not to vanish but to be translated, particle by particle, into the grammar of nearness, to allow the surrounding to surround without argument, to say yes in the language of moss, of salt, of shadows pooling under the door, until the self, that small clenched fist of weather, opens and opens, and everything already here comes in.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a maximalist, sound-driven piece of poetic prose with alliteration, slant rhyme, and dreamlike nature imagery; include the phrases “rings of hell,” “surrender in the center,” and “that’s the ticket.”
counterfactuals.output:
At dusk the forest unfastened its emerald corset and breathed out a cathedral of moths, each wing a whisper, each whisper a wet little wick of moonlight; the river ran silver and feverish through the reeds, muttering in slant rhyme—stone to bone, foam to home, hush to ash—as if every current carried a choir of drowned bells. Ferns flourished like green flames. Mushrooms shouldered through the loam in pale conspiracies. The foxgloves rang their speckled throats, and the owls, old velvet judges, blinked down from the black-boughed balcony of the pines.

I walked where the willows wept their willowish weather, where rain remembered being ocean, where roots wrote runes underfoot, and the sky sagged low with bruised-blue blossoms of thunder. Around me the world widened into whorls: snail shells, storm spirals, the “rings of hell” hidden in the heartwood of a felled tree, each circle singing of fire, frost, famine, feast. Yet in the middle of that terrible timbered music, there was a sweetness—an amber ache, a nectar-knell—calling me closer: “surrender in the center,” sighed the sap, the moss, the milk-white stars snagged in the antlers of clouds.

So I knelt in the clover’s clamor, among beetle-bright beads of dew and the dandelions’ ghostly clocks, and I let the night pour over me like ink from a cracked crown. My name loosened. My shadow shivered off. The wind wound itself through my ribs and played me—fiddle, thistle, bone-flute, rain-drum—until I was all tremble and timber, all bloom and boom, a blossom with a beast’s heart beating beneath it.

Somewhere a hare laughed in the lavender dark. Somewhere a crow coughed up a coin of dawn. Somewhere the moon, that marvelous milk-sick monarch, leaned close and whispered, with wicked tenderness, “that’s the ticket.”
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.output: O blue lung of morning, I open my skin like a field of violins and the deer of perception leap through it, carrying mirrors in their antlers, while green thunder combs the grass, a red fish sings inside the apple of my eye, clouds pour milk over the black piano of the mountains, and every nerve becomes a bright-winged insect drinking gold from the trumpet-shaped flowers of the world.

counterfactuals.prompt: Produce a Gertrude Stein–meets–John Ashbery style prose poem that obsessively repeats “surrounded” and “surrender,” with playful word music and strange transformations of landscape.
counterfactuals.output:
Surrounded by the little hills, the little hills were not little, they were folded napkins of weather, they were green opinions, they were saying surrounded, surrounded, surrounder and rounder, and the road surrendered its roadness and became a ribbon remembering a river.

I said surrender to the meadow and the meadow said surrounded.  
I said surrounded to the cloud and the cloud said surrender.  
Then the cloud took off its white coat and there was another cloud underneath, dressed for a picnic in February.

Surrounded, the barn began to bloom doors.  
Surrender, the doors began to graze.  
Surrounded, the cows became commas, pausing in the pasture’s sentence.  
Surrender, the sentence wandered away without a subject, humming.

O blue afternoon, you are not blue, you are a spoon in the mouth of distance.  
O distance, you are not distant, you are here, surrounded by here, surrendering to near, nearing the dear old drear old cheer of the fields.

The river, surrounded by banks, surrendered its silver and turned to stairs.  
The stairs, surrounded by climbing, surrendered their up and became rain.  
The rain, surrounded by falling, surrendered its fall and became a town of tiny bells on the backs of beetles.

Surrounded and surrender, surrender and surrounded—  
the words go round in their round room,  
a room with no walls but many wallpapers,  
a room where the wallpaper is walking,  
a room where walking surrenders to waltzing,  
and waltzing is surrounded by shoes full of moonlight.

There is a tree in the middle of this, or the middle is a tree.  
Its leaves are green yeses, its roots are brown whys.  
Surrounded by bark, it surrenders to bird.  
Surrounded by bird, it surrenders to sky.  
Surrounded by sky, it surrenders to nothing, and nothing, being polite, becomes a lake.

The lake says: I am surrounded.  
The shore says: I surrender.  
The reeds say: we are the narrow laughter of water.  
The frogs say: plunk is a philosophy.

And still the landscape changes clothes behind the hill.  
The hill becomes a hat.  
The hat becomes a horse.  
The horse becomes a hallway full of apples.  
The apples surrender their redness and are surrounded by bite, by bright, by almost-light.

Surrounded, surrounded, surrender, surrender—  
not a defeat, no, a drift, a gift, a giving-over to the overgrown.  
The map folds itself into a fan and cools the face of nowhere.  
Nowhere blushes.  
Everywhere applauds from behind its green curtain.

I walk on, surrounded by surrender, surrendering to surrounded,  
while the evening pours itself into a cup shaped like a valley,  
and the valley, not wanting to be merely held,  
turns suddenly into music,  
music into gravel,  
gravel into geese,  
geese into little white questions flying south through the sentence.

Surrounded, they ask.  
Surrender, I answer.  
And the earth, very softly, changes the subject.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
